title: Combination of CDK 4/6 Inhibitor Palbociclib with Rapamycin Synergistically Inhibits Growth of  Hepatocellular Carcinoma in Preclinical Models
content: Background: Although CDK4/6 inhibition suppresses HCC growth, compensatory mTOR signaling may limit its efficacy. We evaluated the antitumor activity and mechanistic effects of combining the CDK4/6 inhibitor palbociclib with the mTOR inhibitor rapamycin. Methods: Drug activity and in-teraction were assessed in SNU-398 and HuH-7 cells using cell confluence and viability assays, combination-index analysis, flow cytometry, and immunoblotting. Efficacy was evaluated in HuH-7 xenografts and an immunocompetent c-MET/β-catenin-driven HCC model generated by hydro-dynamic tail-vein injection (HTVI). Tumor growth, time to a prespecified tumor-volume endpoint, plasma alpha-fetoprotein (AFP), and liver weight were measured. RNA sequencing with gene-set enrichment analysis, immunoblotting, and TUNEL staining were used to characterize pathway activity and apoptosis. Results: Palbociclib inhibited proliferation more potently than sorafenib, reduced RB phosphorylation, increased endogenous CDK inhibitors, and activated mTOR-pathway proteins; rapamycin abrogated this compensatory signaling. All combination-index values were <1, indicating synergistic growth inhibition. Combined treatment enhanced G1 arrest and sustained proliferation suppression. In xenografts, the combination significantly reduced tumor-specific growth rate and prolonged time to the tumor-volume endpoint versus all other groups. In the HTVI model, the combination most effectively limited AFP progression, increased AFP doubling time, and reduced liver weight toward normal. Across models, combination maximally suppressed cell-cycle and mTORC1 signaling, increased tumor-cell apoptosis, and produced liver func-tion-related transcriptional profiles closest to normal liver. Conclusion: Combined palbociclib and rapamycin produces synergistic growth inhibition in vitro with enhanced antitumor activity in vivo, consistent with overcoming palbociclib-induced compensatory mTOR signaling. These find-ings support further study of dual CDK4/6–mTOR inhibition for HCC.
